headline: Rescued Gorilla Gives Birth in Congo Park, Signaling Species Recovery
meta_description: A reintroduced Grauer's gorilla who was rescued from trafficking has given birth in Virunga National Park, offering hope for a critically endangered species.
summary_short: Lulingu, rescued from illegal wildlife trafficking a decade ago, has successfully given birth in the wild—a milestone for the critically endangered Grauer's gorilla.
body:
In May 2026, Lulingu, a Grauer's gorilla reintroduced to Virunga National Park in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, gave birth to a healthy baby—a moment that conservationists say signals genuine hope for a species on the brink of extinction. The birth matters because it proves that rescued gorillas can not only survive in the wild, but thrive and reproduce there. "The baby and the mother are doing perfectly well," said Jackson Kabuyaya Mbeke, country director of the DRC Gorilla Rehabilitation and Conservation Education Center (GRACE). "It really makes us happy. We are proud of her, it is also a bit of our success. Imagine, we knew her as a baby, we watched her grow, be rehabilitated and now she is a mother."

Lulingu's journey began in 2016 when she arrived at GRACE, a 16-hectare sanctuary, at just 18 months old after being rescued from an illegal wildlife trafficking network by the Congolese Wildlife Authority and the NGO Gorilla Doctors. For years, she was cared for by adoptive gorilla mothers in an environment mimicking her natural habitat, before being released near Mount Tshiaberimu in Virunga. Her successful motherhood demonstrates that rehabilitation and reintroduction can work—and that gorillas removed from the wild can adapt and contribute to population recovery.

The stakes are stark. Grauer's gorilla, the world's largest primate and found only in eastern DRC's tropical forests, has been classified as critically endangered since 2016. An estimated 77 percent of the population vanished between 1994 and 2015, collapsing from roughly 16,900 individuals to just 3,800. Every birth now counts. Conservationists are already exploring whether to reintroduce more gorillas into the wild, and they plan to involve local communities in naming Lulingu's baby—a step toward building support for conservation in a region facing ongoing conflict and poaching.
quick_facts: Lulingu rescued from trafficking in 2016 at 18 months old
Gave birth May 2026 in Virunga National Park, DRC
GRACE sanctuary spans 16 hectares in eastern Congo
Species reclassified as critically endangered in 2016
